bigPicture: The developer is becoming a manager: as AI coding tools get massively more capable (Codex with browser, memory, plugins; Opus 4.7 with adaptive thinking), the evidence shows humans shifting from writing code to reviewing it — and using MORE AI, not less, as it improves.

dataPoints.stat: AI tool usage jumped 44% when models improved, confirming a Jevons paradox for coding
dataPoints.context: Cursor's UChicago study found efficiency gains don't reduce AI usage — they compound it. CTOs should budget for accelerating consumption, not savings.

dataPoints.stat: Code review is now the fastest-growing developer task as AI writes more code
dataPoints.context: Cursor's research shows the developer role is shifting from author to editor/manager — a structural change in how engineering teams operate.

dataPoints.stat: OpenAI launched its first domain-specific frontier model (GPT-Rosalind) for biology and drug discovery
dataPoints.context: Signals a new era of vertical frontier models — general-purpose may not be the only game anymore. 12.7K+ engagement suggests massive interest.

dataPoints.stat: Developers adopt better AI models in two phases: more volume first, harder tasks only later
dataPoints.context: Cursor study finding that complexity jumps lag behind adoption — eng managers expecting immediate skill-up are setting wrong expectations.

tldr: Codex got a massive upgrade — browser control, computer use, persistent memory, 90+ plugins, and image generation turn it into a full agentic coding environment, not just an autocomplete.
Opus 4.7 requires real workflow changes: adaptive thinking replaces fixed budgets, version mismatches kill quality, and Boris Cherny says verification loops are the #1 lever for output quality.

The Cursor/UChicago study is the first rigorous evidence that better AI models create a Jevons paradox — developers use MORE AI, shift to reviewing over writing, and only tackle harder problems after a volume-first phase.
OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind marks the start of domain-specific frontier models, while Anthropic's platform play (per Mostaque) is about owning the workflow wrapper, not just the model layer.

Google shipped multilingual TTS in Gemini 3.1 Flash, and the LangGraph/LangSmith ecosystem keeps maturing with Cisco reference architectures and reusable evaluator templates — enterprise multi-agent infrastructure is solidifying fast.

contentFuel.author: bcherny
contentFuel.content:
6/ Give Claude a way to verify its work

Finally, make sure Claude has a way to verify its work. This has always been a way to 2-3x what you get out of Claude, and with 4.7 it's more important than ever.

Verification looks different depending on the task. For backend work, make sure Claude knows how to start up your server/service to test it end to end; for frontend work, use the Claude Chromium extension to give Claude a way to control your browser; for desktop apps, use computer use.

contentFuel.author: bcherny
contentFuel.content:
5/ Configure your effort level

Opus 4.7 uses adaptive thinking instead of thinking budgets. To tune the model to think more/less, we recommend tuning effort.

Use lower effort for faster responses and lower token usage. Use higher effort for the most intelligence and capability.

Personally, I use xhigh effort for most tasks, and max effort for the hardest tasks. Max applies to just your current session; other effort levels are sticky and persist for your next session also.
